questions.answer: I do, actually. My work involves a fair bit of writing, and I've grown to enjoy shaping ideas into clear, [[coherent]] sentences. I sometimes jot down thoughts in a notebook too, just for myself.

questions.q: Did you enjoy writing when you were at school?
questions.answer: Not especially, to be honest. Essay writing felt like a chore because we mostly had to memorise model answers. It was only at university that I started to enjoy it, once I could [[articulate]] my own ideas rather than copying someone else's.

questions.q: Do you often write emails or letters?
questions.answer: Emails, yes, mostly for work. Handwritten letters have almost disappeared, which is a shame. There's a personal warmth to a letter that a quick email just can't quite [[replicate]].

questions.q: Have you ever written a poem or a story?
questions.answer: Only a few short poems in Bengali when I was a teenager, mostly about the river and the monsoon. They were fairly [[sentimental]], looking back, but I still keep them in an old notebook at home.

questions.q: Do you think handwriting will still be important in the future?
questions.answer: Less than before, certainly, since so much is typed now. Still, I think it will always matter to some degree. A handwritten note has a personal touch, and writing by hand helps ideas [[sink in]] far better than typing does.
